review.market_summary: 1) The Fed has turned hawkish. It raised rates for the first time since 2023, and Waller is now openly floating a 50bp hike in December. A strong October jobs report (+165k, unemployment 4.1%) backs him up. This is the main signal, but the market isn't fully buying it yet: SPY, QQQ and IWM are flat to up over 5 days, the dollar (UUP) hasn't moved, and long bonds (TLT) are slightly up. 2) Nvidia's 'Huang scandal' is pushing Congress toward a full ban on AI chip exports to China, and Republicans are now joining in. NVDA has already fallen 11.6% to its most oversold level since 2019, while AMD has rallied 8.9% even though it faces the same China export risk. 3) Iran de-escalation has pushed Brent below $90. USO, XLE and JETS have each moved 8-9% in a week, so that trade is mostly done. Overall: three of the four headline themes are already in prices. The cleanest gap left is the hawkish Fed against flat rate-sensitive assets. Keep total exposure to the hawkish-Fed idea small, because UUP and TLT are related bets.
